This article elaborates how to identify and evaluate causal factors to improve scientific impact. Currently, analyzing scientific impact can be beneficial to various academic activities including funding application, mentor recommendation, discovering potential cooperators, and the like. It is universally acknowledged that high-impact scholars often have more opportunities to receive awards as an encouragement for their hard work. Therefore, scholars spend great efforts in making scientific achievements and improving scientific impact during their academic life. However, what are the determinate factors that control scholars’ academic success? The answer to this question can help scholars conduct their research more efficiently. Under this consideration, our article presents and analyzes the causal factors that are crucial for scholars’ academic success. We first propose five major factors including article-centered factors, author-centered factors, venue-centered factors, institution-centered factors, and temporal factors. Then, we apply recent advanced machine learning algorithms and jackknife method to assess the importance of each causal factor. Our empirical results show that author-centered and article-centered factors have the highest relevancy to scholars’ future success in the computer science area. result.paraphrase: This article explains how to identify and assess causal factors for improving scientific impact. Analyzing scientific impact can currently support many academic tasks, such as funding applications, mentor recommendations, and finding potential collaborators. It is widely recognized that high-impact scholars often have more chances to receive awards in recognition of their hard work. As a result, scholars devote substantial effort to producing academic achievements and enhancing their scientific impact throughout their careers. But which determinants control scholars’ academic success? Answering this question can help scholars carry out research more efficiently. With this in mind, the article presents and examines the causal factors that are essential to scholars’ academic success. We first identify five main factors: article-centered, author-centered, venue-centered, institution-centered, and temporal factors. Next, we use recent advanced machine learning algorithms and the jackknife method to evaluate the importance of each causal factor. Our empirical findings indicate that author-centered and article-centered factors are most strongly related to scholars’ future success in computer science. In addition, we observe an interesting phenomenon: scholars’ h-index values within the same institution or university are actually very close to one another.
